issue_title: toJSONSchema emits a base64url pattern that accepts strings z.base64url() rejects
issue_body:
### Problem

`z.base64url()` and the JSON Schema it generates disagree about the same string:

```ts
z.base64url().safeParse("A").success;              // false
z.toJSONSchema(z.base64url()).pattern;             // "^[A-Za-z0-9_-]*$"  — matches "A"
```

Unpadded base64url encodes 3 bytes per 4 characters, so a length that leaves a remainder of 1 mod 4 carries no whole byte and no encoder can produce it. `regexes.base64` already rules this out; `regexes.base64url` does not.

`isValidBase64URL()` catches it at parse time, so `parse()` is correct. But `$ZodBase64URL` assigns the loose regex to `def.pattern`, and that is what `toJSONSchema()` emits — so a consumer validating against the generated schema accepts input Zod itself rejects. That matters where the schema is handed to something else (tool calling, a gateway) and Zod re-validates afterwards.

### Suggested fix

Give `base64url` the same split `base64` already has — a strict pattern for the schema, a dedicated validator for parsing:

- `regexes.base64url` → `/^(?:[A-Za-z0-9_-]{4})*(?:[A-Za-z0-9_-]{2,3})?$/`, mirroring `regexes.base64`. This is what lands in `def.pattern`.
- a new `regexes.base64urlCharset` (`/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/`) for `isValidBase64URL()`.

The second part is load-bearing: `isValidBase64()` never runs its pattern (it checks `length % 4` and calls `atob`), but `isValidBase64URL()` does run its own against user input of any size, and a quantified group overflows the stack on a long subject — the existing `big base64 and base64url` test (10 MB) hits exactly that. The length rule is already enforced downstream, where the padded string reaches `isValidBase64()`.

### Status

I have this implemented on a branch, with `"A"` added to the existing invalid fixtures in `string.test.ts`. `check:semver`, `check:comments`, `biome check` and the full `packages/zod` suite (7835 tests) pass, and runtime parse behaviour is unchanged.

The change is here, ready to open as a PR: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/compare/main...oleg6k:zod:fix/base64url-pattern

PR creation is currently limited to collaborators, so I am filing this instead — happy to open the PR as soon as that lifts, or to hand over the diff if someone wants to land it directly.

issue_title: z.emoji() accepts strings that contain no emoji
issue_body:
### Problem

`z.emoji()` accepts strings that contain no emoji at all:

```ts
z.emoji().parse("123");        // passes
z.emoji().parse("#");          // passes
z.emoji().parse("*");          // passes
z.emoji().parse("\u{200D}");   // lone ZWJ, passes
z.emoji().parse("\u{FE0F}");   // lone variation selector, passes
z.emoji().parse("\u{1F3FD}");  // lone skin tone modifier, passes
```

The pattern is `^[\p{Extended_Pictographic}\p{Emoji_Component}]+$`. `\p{Emoji_Component}` is not a set of emoji — it is the set of pieces that combine with one: ASCII digits `0`–`9`, `#`, `*`, regional indicators, skin tone modifiers, ZWJ and variation selectors. A string built only from components is not an emoji.

### Suggested fix

Keep the character class exactly as it is — the single class matters, #6347 replaced an alternation with it to kill the exponential backtracking over the U+1F9B0–U+1F9B3 overlap — and add a leading lookahead requiring one anchor: an `Extended_Pictographic`, a regional indicator, or U+20E3, the enclosing keycap that makes `1️⃣` an emoji.

```
^(?=[\s\S]*[\p{Extended_Pictographic}\p{Regional_Indicator}⃣])[\p{Extended_Pictographic}\p{Emoji_Component}]+$
```

`[\s\S]` rather than `[^]`, and `⃣` rather than `\u{20E3}`, because the pattern is emitted into JSON Schema and not every consumer parses the ECMAScript-only spellings.

### Checks

- every emoji in `unicode-emoji-json` (1914 entries) still validates, and every existing fixture in `string.test.ts` passes, keycap sequences included
- `recheck` reports the new pattern safe; the lookahead is a single unnested quantifier, so matching stays linear — measured at 1k/10k/50k characters, on both the matching and the failing path, it costs about 10% more than the current pattern and scales linearly
- two snapshots that carry the pattern as text need updating
- full `packages/zod` suite passes (7835 tests)

### Status

Implemented on a branch with tests for the component-only cases above. The change is here, ready to open as a PR: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/compare/main...oleg6k:zod:fix/emoji-component-only

PR creation is currently limited to collaborators, so I am filing this instead — happy to open the PR as soon as that lifts.

issue_title: fromJSONSchema silently ignores minProperties and maxProperties
issue_body:
## `fromJSONSchema` silently ignores `minProperties` and `maxProperties`

Both keywords are listed in `RECOGNIZED_KEYS` in `from-json-schema.ts` (so they are silently consumed instead of falling into `extraMeta`), but no validation logic is ever attached to the resulting schema. An object with `minProperties: 1` accepts `{}`, and one with `maxProperties: 2` accepts three or more keys without error.

### Reproduce

```ts
import { fromJSONSchema } from "zod/v4";

const schema = fromJSONSchema({
  type: "object",
  properties: { a: { type: "string" }, b: { type: "number" } },
  minProperties: 1,
  maxProperties: 2,
});

schema.safeParse({}).success      // true  — should be false (0 < minProperties)
schema.safeParse({ a: "x", b: 1, c: true }).success  // true  — should be false (3 > maxProperties)
```

### Expected

Both should fail: `{}` has 0 properties (< `minProperties: 1`), and `{ a, b, c }` has 3 properties (> `maxProperties: 2`).

### Actual

Both parse successfully — the keywords are consumed without effect.

### Root cause

`minProperties` and `maxProperties` appear in the `RECOGNIZED_KEYS` set (lines 62–63 of `from-json-schema.ts`) but are never referenced in `convertBaseSchema` or `convertSchema`. By contrast, the analogous array keywords `minItems`/`maxItems` are applied via `.check(z.minLength(...))` / `.check(z.maxLength(...))`, and string `minLength`/`maxLength` via `.min()` / `.max()`. The object property-count keywords simply have no corresponding branch.

### Fix

Layer a `.check()` on the object schema after `propertyNames` handling, counting `Object.keys(value).length` against the threshold and emitting `too_small` / `too_big` issues with `origin: "object"`. I have a patch ready (37 lines in `from-json-schema.ts` + 40 lines of regression tests in `from-json-schema.test.ts`) — happy to open a PR if `pull_request_creation_policy` allows, or I can attach the diff here.

issue_title: z.url(), z.ipv6() and z.cidrv6() accept ASCII tab/newline because the URL parser deletes them
issue_body:
`z.url()`, `z.httpUrl()`, `z.ipv6()` and `z.cidrv6()` all validate by calling `new URL()` and treating "didn't throw" as valid. Step 2 of the WHATWG basic URL parser **deletes** every ASCII tab, LF and CR from the input before parsing — it flags a validation error but recovers rather than failing — so `new URL()` succeeds on strings containing them and reports on a string that isn't the one it was given.

On 4.4.3:

```ts
z.ipv6().parse("::1\n");                    // "::1\n"     — net.isIPv6() says false
z.cidrv6().parse("::1\n/64");               // "::1\n/64"
z.url().parse("https://exa\nmple.com");     // "https://exa\nmple.com"
z.httpUrl().parse("https://exa\nmple.com"); // "https://exa\nmple.com"
```

The host case is the sharp one: `new URL("https://exa\nmple.com").host` is `example.com`, so the string Zod validated and the string Zod returned are URLs pointing at different hosts.

Tab, LF and CR are the only characters with this property. I enumerated all 32 C0 controls at host, path, query, fragment, leading and trailing positions: every other one is either percent-encoded (`https://example.com/pa%00th`) or rejected, and U+0009/U+000A/U+000D are the only three that can be injected into the **host** and still validate.

It also breaks a self-consistency invariant — `regexes.ipv6` is still emitted as the `pattern` by `toJSONSchema()`, and it rejects these:

```ts
new RegExp(z.toJSONSchema(z.ipv6()).pattern).test("::1\n"); // false
z.ipv6().safeParse("::1\n").success;                        // true
```

I scanned every code point 0x0000–0x10FFFF inserted into `::1` and `::1/64`: `z.ipv6()` disagrees with `net.isIPv6` on exactly those three characters and nothing else.

`isValidBase64` already handles the identical hazard one section down — "atob ignores whitespace, so reject it up front" — so the shape of the fix is settled by precedent: scan for `[\t\n\r]` ahead of each `new URL()` call. Happy to open a PR.

issue_title: fromJSONSchema: propertyNames with enum is treated as required keys
issue_body:
### Summary

`z.fromJSONSchema()` converts an object schema that constrains its keys with
`propertyNames: { enum: [...] }` into a Zod schema where each enum value becomes a
**required** property. `propertyNames` restricts which key *names are allowed*; it
does not make any key *required*. As a result, a valid object that contains only a
subset of the allowed keys is incorrectly rejected.

### Zod version

`zod@4.4.3` (Node 20)

### Reproduction

```js
import { z } from "zod";

const schema = {
  type: "object",
  propertyNames: { enum: ["a", "b"] },
  additionalProperties: { type: "string" },
};

const zodSchema = z.fromJSONSchema(schema);

// `{ a: "x" }` is valid against the JSON Schema (an allowed key, string value),
// but Zod rejects it:
zodSchema.parse({ a: "x" });
// ✖ ZodError: [{ path: ["b"], code: "invalid_type",
//     message: "Invalid input: expected string, received undefined" }]
```

### What's happening

Round-tripping the converted schema back through `z.toJSONSchema()` shows the enum
property names were turned into `required`:

```jsonc
{
  "type": "object",
  "propertyNames": { "type": "string", "enum": ["a", "b"] },
  "additionalProperties": { "type": "string" },
  "required": ["a", "b"]   // ← injected; not present in the source schema
}
```

### Expected

- `{ a: "x" }` and `{ b: "y" }` should pass (as should `{}`, unless `minProperties`
  or an explicit `required` say otherwise).
- Only keys *not* in `["a", "b"]` should fail (via `propertyNames`).
- No property should be required unless it appears in the schema's own `required`.

### Notes

This looks like the object-keyword sibling of #6200 (`fromJSONSchema` requiring
`prefixItems` tuple elements when `minItems` is omitted) — both over-require
members that the source schema leaves optional.

issue_title: fromJSONSchema date-time rejects valid RFC 3339 offsets
issue_body:
`fromJSONSchema({ type: "string", format: "date-time" })` currently maps to `z.iso.datetime()` and rejects valid RFC 3339 timestamps with numeric UTC offsets.

```ts
const schema = z.fromJSONSchema({ type: "string", format: "date-time" });

schema.parse("2026-07-29T14:30:00Z"); // accepted
schema.parse("2026-07-29T16:30:00+02:00"); // rejected
```

JSON Schema defines `date-time` using RFC 3339, where both `Z` and numeric offsets are valid. A local timestamp without an offset should remain invalid.

The mapping can preserve that behavior by using `z.iso.datetime({ offset: true })`. Authored JSON Schema constraints such as `pattern` should continue to compose with the format check.

issue_title: fromJSONSchema requires prefixItems tuple elements when minItems is omitted
issue_body:
## Summary

`fromJSONSchema` converts JSON Schema tuple-style array schemas into Zod required tuples. As a result, arrays shorter than the number of positional schemas are rejected even when the JSON Schema does not set `minItems`.

In JSON Schema, `prefixItems` / draft-7 array-form `items` constrain the elements that are present. They do not make every positional schema required unless `minItems` says so.

## Code path

- `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/from-json-schema.ts`: `prefixItems` is mapped to `z.tuple(...)`.
- `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/from-json-schema.ts`: draft-7 array-form `items` is also mapped to `z.tuple(...)`.
- `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/from-json-schema.test.ts`: the current `prefixItems` test expects a shorter array to throw, which appears stricter than JSON Schema semantics.

## Steps to reproduce

Checked against `912f0f51b0ced654d0069741e7160834dca742ee`.

### Draft 2020-12 `prefixItems`

```ts
import { fromJSONSchema } from "zod/v4";

const schema = fromJSONSchema({
  $schema: "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  type: "array",
  prefixItems: [{ type: "string" }],
});

console.log(schema.safeParse([]).success);
console.log(schema.safeParse(["ok"]).success);
```

Actual output:

```txt
false
true
```

Expected output:

```txt
true
true
```

### Draft-7 array-form `items`

```ts
import { fromJSONSchema } from "zod/v4";

const schema = fromJSONSchema({
  $schema: "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  type: "array",
  items: [{ type: "string" }],
  additionalItems: false,
});

console.log(schema.safeParse([]).success);
console.log(schema.safeParse(["ok"]).success);
console.log(schema.safeParse(["ok", "extra"]).success);
```

Actual output:

```txt
false
true
false
```

Expected output:

```txt
true
true
false
```

## Expected behavior

Without `minItems`, shorter arrays should be valid as long as every present positional item satisfies its schema.

For example:

- `prefixItems: [{ type: "string" }]` should accept `[]` and `["ok"]`.
- draft-7 `items: [{ type: "string" }], additionalItems: false` should accept `[]` and `["ok"]`, but reject `["ok", "extra"]`.

## Actual behavior

The generated Zod schema rejects `[]` because `z.tuple([z.string()])` requires the first tuple element to be present.

## Existing coverage

Related open PRs exist, but they appear to cover the trailing/rest side rather than the shorter-array side:

- #6020 fixes open-by-default tuple rest behavior for omitted `items` / `additionalItems`.
- #6023 fixes boolean `true` rest behavior for `items: true` / `additionalItems: true`.

Both directions are related, but adding `.rest(...)` to `z.tuple([z.string()])` still leaves the first tuple element required, so arrays shorter than the prefix length remain rejected unless the fix also changes required-prefix handling.

#6193 / #6194 are about `toJSONSchema()` emitting length constraints for closed Zod tuples, which is the opposite conversion direction.

## Suggested fix

When JSON Schema does not set `minItems` to require all positional schemas, avoid representing `prefixItems` / array-form `items` as a required-length Zod tuple directly.

The converted schema should:

- validate each present positional element against its corresponding schema;
- allow shorter arrays down to the JSON Schema `minItems` value, defaulting to `0`;
- still enforce `items:false` / `additionalItems:false` for elements beyond the positional schema list;
- preserve typed rest behavior when `items` / `additionalItems` is a schema object.

## Suggested tests

- 2020-12 `prefixItems: [{ type: "string" }]` with no `minItems` accepts `[]`.
- 2020-12 `prefixItems: [{ type: "string" }, { type: "number" }]` with no `minItems` accepts `[]` and `["ok"]`.
- A present prefix item with the wrong type still fails, e.g. `[1]` for `{ type: "string" }`.
- draft-7 `items: [{ type: "string" }], additionalItems:false` accepts `[]` and `["ok"]`, but rejects `["ok", "extra"]`.
- Adding `minItems: 1` rejects `[]`, while adding `minItems: 2` rejects arrays shorter than two items.

---
Submitted with Codex.

issue_title: fromJSONSchema ignores additionalProperties:false when patternProperties is present
issue_body:
## Summary

`fromJSONSchema` accepts object properties that match neither `properties` nor `patternProperties` when the source JSON Schema sets `additionalProperties: false`, as long as `patternProperties` is present. This makes the generated Zod schema more permissive than the source JSON Schema.

## Code path

- `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/from-json-schema.ts`: the `patternProperties` branch builds loose records and returns from that branch.
- `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/from-json-schema.ts`: the later `additionalProperties === false` handling is only reached when the earlier `patternProperties` branch is not taken.

## Steps to reproduce

Checked against `912f0f51b0ced654d0069741e7160834dca742ee`.

```ts
import { fromJSONSchema } from "zod/v4";

const schema = fromJSONSchema({
  type: "object",
  patternProperties: {
    "^S_": { type: "string" },
  },
  additionalProperties: false,
});

console.log(schema.safeParse({ S_name: "ok" }).success);
console.log(schema.safeParse({ X_A: false }).success);
```

Actual output:

```txt
true
true
```

## Expected behavior

The second parse should fail. `X_A` does not match `^S_`, so it is an additional property. With `additionalProperties: false`, JSON Schema rejects properties that match neither `properties` nor `patternProperties`.

Expected output:

```txt
true
false
```

## Actual behavior

The generated Zod schema accepts `{ X_A: false }`.

## Existing coverage

I found related but not equivalent coverage:

- #5449 covered adding general `patternProperties` support.
- #5702 covers an `allOf` + `additionalProperties: false` interaction.

I did not find an issue or PR covering the `patternProperties` + `additionalProperties: false` interaction above.

## Suggested fix

Apply `additionalProperties` after accounting for keys matched by `properties` and `patternProperties`, instead of returning from the `patternProperties` branch before the `additionalProperties` logic runs.

## Suggested tests

- `fromJSONSchema({ type: "object", patternProperties: { "^S_": { type: "string" } }, additionalProperties: false })` accepts `{ S_name: "ok" }`.
- The same schema rejects `{ X_A: false }`.
- A matching pattern key with the wrong value type, such as `{ S_name: 1 }`, still fails.

---
Submitted with Codex.

issue_title: v4: `.length()` / `.size()` error messages ignore the `exact` flag
issue_body:
## Zod version

v4.4.3

## Minimal reproduction

```ts
import { z } from "zod";

z.string().length(4).parse("abc");
```

## Expected

Since `.length(4)` represents an exact constraint, the error message should indicate that the expected length is **exactly 4**, as it did in Zod v3.

## Actual

The error message uses range wording (e.g. `>=4` / `<=4`), even though the generated issue already contains `exact: true`.

## Additional context

While investigating this, I found that:

* `exact: true` is assigned for fixed-length validations in `core/checks.ts`.
* `exact` is part of the `too_small` / `too_big` issue types.
* None of the v4 locale renderers currently use `issue.exact` when formatting messages.
* The v3 English locale did use `issue.exact` to produce messages such as "exactly 4".
* I couldn't find an existing issue or PR covering this behavior.

Before opening a PR, I'd like to confirm whether this is an unintended regression. If so, I'd be happy to submit a focused PR updating the English locale together with the relevant tests.

issue_title: toJSONSchema(schemaRegistry, opts) is very slow with a large registry
issue_body:
As I add more types to a schema registry, calling `toJSONSchema` on that registry gets very slow, growing much faster than the growth in the size of the registry.

In a private repo I have, a registry with only about 3000 types in it takes 30 seconds to process on a MacBook M3.

I've collected some perf dumps, and the problem might be coming from one or both of these places:

### Finalize iteration

`finalize` is called on every schema, but for each schema it goes through all of the refs and checks each one:

https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/zod/src/v4/core/to-json-schema.ts#L449

A lot of that ends up being noop, as everything only needs to be procesesd once.  But it's still building all of those new arrays for iteration and revisiting every member of `ctx.seen` many times over.

When I hack my copy of zod to only run this loop once per context, the schema generation time for my example goes down from about 30s to about 18s.

### Nested parent computation

When a schema has a parent, registry get walks the chain recursively to get ancestor data:

https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/zod/src/v4/core/registries.ts#L65

This data can be recomputed many times as registry get is called many times, even though no registry data is written during the process.

When I add a subclass of $ZodRegistry that can cache the results of these get calls, the schema generation time for my example goes down from about 30s to about 20s.

issue_title: `looseRecord` with a closed key schema reports unrecognized keys fatally
issue_body:
This fails to parse:


```js
const A = z.looseRecord(z.enum(['foo', 'bar']), z.any())
A.parse({ foo: 123, bar: {}, baz: null })
```

This parses:

```js
const A = z.looseRecord(z.string().regex(/^foo|bar$/), z.any())
A.parse({ foo: 123, bar: {}, baz: null })
```

Reason: record's implementation (which looseRecord also uses) attempts to retrieve the closed schema value set with `def.keyType._zod.values`.

`z.enum` provides it. `z.regex` doesn't attempt to analyze the regex to provide it. Therefore, the false branch triggers with the rechex, in which `ctx.issues.push` is under `def.mode === "loose"`. The true branch has no such condition, meaning `unrecognized_key` is always reported.

https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/c7805073fef5b6b8857307c3d4b3597a70613bc2/packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts#L2773-L2854

@pullfrog also signaled this in #5666.

issue_title: treeifyError throws TypeError when an issue path contains a key inherited from Object.prototype (e.g. toString)
issue_body:
`treeifyError` throws a `TypeError` whenever a validation issue's `path` contains a segment whose name matches a property inherited from `Object.prototype` (for example `toString`, `valueOf`, `constructor`, or `hasOwnProperty`).

Minimal reproduction:

```
import zod, { treeifyError } from 'zod';

const schema = zod.object({ toString: zod.string() });
const result = schema.safeParse({}); // success: false

if (!result.success) {
    treeifyError(result.error); // throws TypeError
}
```

The parse correctly fails: `{}.toString` resolves to the inherited `Object.prototype.toString` function, so the `toString` field is reported as `invalid_type (expected string, received function)` with `path: ["toString"]`. That part is expected. The bug is that `treeifyError` then throws while building the tree:

```
node_modules/zod/v4/core/errors.js:113
                        curr.errors.push(mapper(issue));
                                    ^
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'push')
    at processError (node_modules/zod/v4/core/errors.js:113:37)
    at treeifyError (node_modules/zod/v4/core/errors.js:120:5)
```

Root cause:

`treeifyError` builds the tree using a plain object as a dictionary:

```
curr.properties ?? (curr.properties = {});
(_a = curr.properties)[el] ?? (_a[el] = { errors: [] });
curr = curr.properties[el];
```

When the path segment `el` is an `Object.prototype` key, `curr.properties[el]` returns the inherited member (e.g. the `toString` function) instead of `undefined`. The `??` short-circuits, so the node is never created, and `curr` is assigned the inherited function which has no `errors` array. The following `curr.errors.push(...)` then throws.
A null-prototype object (`Object.create(null)`) or a `Map` for `properties`, or an `Object.hasOwn` guard, would fix it.

Environment:

issue_title: regexes.domain is missing RFC 1035 length limits
issue_body:
## Context

`regexes.domain` (used by `z.httpUrl()` for the URL host check) currently has no length anchors:

```ts
export const domain: RegExp = /^([a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?\.)+[a-zA-Z]{2,}$/;
```

vs. `regexes.hostname` (used by `z.hostname()`), which does enforce the RFC 1035 limits:

```ts
export const hostname: RegExp =
  /^(?=.{1,253}\.?$)[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[-0-9a-zA-Z]{0,61}[0-9a-zA-Z])?)*\.?$/;
```

So `z.httpUrl()` accepts hosts that exceed the 253-character total or have non-TLD labels longer than 63 characters, while `z.hostname()` rejects them.

## Question

Is this an intentional looseness for `z.httpUrl()` (since RFC 3986 / WHATWG URL doesn't itself impose DNS length limits, even though the underlying DNS does), or a gap worth closing?

If the latter, the fix is small — adding a `(?=.{1,253}\.?$)` lookahead and capping the TLD with a `{2,63}` quantifier. Happy to follow up with a PR if there's interest.

## Note

This is independent from #5963 (underscore support, currently open), but it'd be cleaner to land that first to avoid noisy rebases.

issue_title: `multipleOf` silently accepts non-multiples for small numbers (scientific notation bug in `floatSafeRemainder`)
issue_body:
`z.number().multipleOf(1e-7).safeParse(2.5e-7)` returns `{ success: true }`,  but `2.5e-7 / 1e-7 = 2.5`  (not a whole number).

Repro:
```
z.number().multipleOf(1e-7).safeParse(2.5e-7)  //  { success: true } — should be false
z.number().multipleOf(1e-7).safeParse(3.3e-7)  // { success: true } — should be false
z.number().multipleOf(1e-7).safeParse(3e-7)    // { success: true } — correct
```

Root cause: `floatSafeRemainder` in util.ts counts decimal places by splitting `val.toString()` on ".". For small numbers, JS uses scientific notation: (2.5e-7).toString() gives "2.5e-7", so the fractional part is "5e-7" (length 4) instead of the actual 8 decimal places. 

The function already handles this for the step parameter (lines 251-255) but not for val.

Suggested fix: Apply the same scientific notation regex to val.toString().

Zod version: 4.3.6

issue_title: discriminatedUnion fails on encode() when discriminator is a ZodCodec
issue_body:
## Description

When using `z.discriminatedUnion` with a discriminator field implemented as a `ZodCodec`,
`decode()` works correctly, but `encode()` fails at runtime with
`No matching discriminator`.

This happens even though:

- the types of `decode()` / `encode()` inputs are correct
- the codec itself is fully bidirectional
- the decoded domain object is valid

The issue appears to be that `discriminatedUnion` attempts to select a branch
**before encoding the discriminator field**, using the domain value instead of
the encoded (raw) value.

---

## Reproducible example

```ts
const LiteralTestCodec1 = z.codec(z.literal(1), z.literal('one'), {
    decode: (raw) => 'one' as const,
    encode: (domain) => 1 as const,
})

const LiteralTestCodec2 = z.codec(z.literal(2), z.literal('two'), {
    decode: (raw) => 'two' as const,
    encode: (domain) => 2 as const,
})

const TestUnionSchema = z.discriminatedUnion(
    'type',
    [
        z.object({
            type: LiteralTestCodec1,
            valueString: z.string(),
        }),
        z.object({
            type: LiteralTestCodec2,
            valueNumber: z.number(),
        }),
    ]
)

const domain = TestUnionSchema.decode({
    type: 1,
    valueString: 'test value',
})

const raw = TestUnionSchema.encode({
    type: 'one',
    valueString: 'test value',
})
```

---

## Actual result

`decode()` works correctly.

`encode()` throws the following error:

```json
ZodError: [
  {
    "code": "invalid_union",
    "errors": [],
    "note": "No matching discriminator",
    "discriminator": "type",
    "path": ["type"],
    "message": "Invalid input"
  }
]
```

---

## Expected behavior

Given that:

- the discriminator codec is bidirectional
- `encode()` should produce a valid raw representation

`encode()` is expected to succeed and return:

```ts
{
    type: 1,
    valueString: "test value"
}
```

---

## Notes / Workaround

At the application level, this issue can be worked around by enabling
`{ unionFallback: true }` when creating the `discriminatedUnion`.

This forces Zod to fall back to full union validation instead of the fast
discriminator-based path.

However, this behavior is surprising when combining:

- `z.discriminatedUnion`
- codecs used as discriminator fields
- `encode()` direction

---

## Possible directions

Below are concrete implementation-oriented ideas based on the current internal behavior of `ZodDiscriminatedUnion` (not prescriptions).

### 1. Make discriminator resolution context-aware

Currently, branch selection in `ZodDiscriminatedUnion` is based on a precomputed map:

```ts
const opt = disc.value.get(input?.[def.discriminator] as any);
if (opt) {
  return opt._zod.run(payload, ctx) as any;
}
```

Where `disc` is a `Map` computed once from `propValues`, derived by recursively inspecting each option schema and then cached.

For `ZodCodec`, `propValues` are defined as:

```ts
util.defineLazy(inst._zod, "propValues", () => def.in._zod.propValues);
```

This means:
- discriminator values are taken exclusively from the **`in` schema**
- there is no context available to distinguish `decode` vs `encode`
- during `encode()`, discriminator resolution still relies on *forward* (`in`) values

One possible direction would be to make `propValues` resolution context-aware, for example by turning it into a function that receives encoding direction from the parsing context (e.g. `ctx.direction: "forward" | "backward"`), allowing codecs to expose discriminator values appropriate to the current direction.

---

### 2. Introduce a backward discriminator path

An alternative (more explicit) approach would be to keep the existing fast-path intact, but add a mirrored mechanism for the backward direction:

- introduce `propValuesBackward` (mirroring `propValues`)
- derive it from `def.out` instead of `def.in` for codecs
- build and cache a separate `discBackward` map
- select between `disc` and `discBackward` based on encoding direction

This would preserve:
- current performance characteristics
- clear separation of forward (`decode`) and backward (`encode`) discriminator resolution

while allowing discriminators implemented as codecs to work symmetrically.

---

### Documentation note

Regardless of implementation, this behavior could also be documented explicitly as a current limitation of combining:

- `z.discriminatedUnion`
- codecs used as discriminator fields
- `encode()` direction

See: https://zod.dev/codecs

---

## Question

Is this behavior considered an intentional limitation of `discriminatedUnion`,
or would a change in discriminator resolution (or explicit documentation of the limitation) be acceptable?

If this aligns with the intended direction of the API, I am willing to prepare a PR.

issue_title: Zod triggers unsafe-eval CSP error
issue_body:
Previous issues related to this were closed:
 - https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/4461
 - https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/5041

CSP is a critical security layer that helps prevent XSS, code injection, and other attacks. The unsafe-eval directive specifically allows dynamic code evaluation through functions like eval(), Function(), and setTimeout(string), which are common attack vectors.
Given Zod's widespread adoption and position, having CSP-compliant behavior by default would significantly benefit the ecosystem.

Workaround with `z.config({ jitless: true });` works, but I wouldn't consider it a proper solution:
 - This flag does not have any connection with CSP by itself 
 - This flag is not enabled by default and will require a major rewrite to enable it, since it has to be added in one place 

Please consider providing CSP-compliant behavior by default, as it would significantly benefit the ecosystem.

z.toJSONSchema(z.intersection(

))

compiles to:

{ "allOf": [{
    "type": "object",
    "properties": { "foo": { "type": "boolean" } },
    "required": ["foo"],
    "additionalProperties": false
}, {

    "required": [ "bar" ],

}]}

where `additionalProperties: false` prevents `{ foo: true, bar: false }` from matching at least one of the rules.

`.looseObject` works around this but isn't strict enough for my taste so for now I'm stuck with extending union cases

https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/62bf4e439e287e55c843245b49f8d34b1ad024ee/packages/zod/src/v4/core/to-json-schema.ts#L521-L526

https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/62bf4e439e287e55c843245b49f8d34b1ad024ee/packages/zod/src/v4/core/to-json-schema.ts#L617-L628

It'd be also great if https://zod.dev/json-schema was updated to reflect the caveat of dynamic catch.

Happy to help with a PR if the above makes sense.

---

In the meantime, I [patched](https://pnpm.io/cli/patch) the logic locally like this:

```diff
} catch {
-   throw new Error("Dynamic catch values are not supported in JSON Schema");
+   // Assume that catch does not change the type of the schema
+   // Context: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/5273
+   break;
}
```

It's more like `unrepresentable: "passthrough"` (which does not exist yet) rather than `unrepresentable: "any"`.

issue_title: Tuple Ignoring Default Values
issue_body:
With a defined tuple that has a fixed length of any value, default values of the property are ignored.

```js
const myTuple = z.tuple([z.string(), z.string().default('bravo')]);
const outVar = myTuple.parse(['alpha']); // results in "Invalid input: expected string, received undefined"
```

Expected response would be `['alpha', 'bravo']`. I did also try the following:

```js
const myTuple = z.tuple([z.string(), z.string()]).default([undefined, 'bravo']);
const outVar = myTuple.parse(['alpha']); // results in same error: "Invalid input: expected string, received undefined"
```

Appears to be coming from [v4/core/schemas.ts#2444](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/v4.1.8/packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts#L2444) where `if (i >= input.length) if (i >= optStart) continue;` continues out of the loop before running the parser on the optional tuple property.

This probably isn't a deal breaker as I'd expect the value to be undefined. This problem with this arises when parsing arguments for ZodFunction. There is no way to have an optional param.

Used in function context:
```js
const myFunc = z.function([z.string(), z.string().default('bravo')]).implement((name, company) => console.log(name, company)); // doesn't work

const myFunc = z.function([z.string(), z.string().default('bravo')]).implement((name, company = 'bravo') => console.log(name, company)); //  works only if defining on the async function
```

Defining a default value on the implement function does work, but seems a little anti-pattern. I'd expected a fixed length tuple to return all values or result in an error.

```js
const [ name, company ] = z.tuple([z.string(), z.string().default('bravo')]).parse(['alpha']); // doesn't fail
```

This not failing allows for company to be `undefined` when I'd be expecting a `String` value.
